Customs Act 2023: This instrument is issued under the authority granted by Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This instrument is issued under the authority granted by Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
National Board of Revenue: The issuance of this exemption order is conducted in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Pesticide: The exemption applies to specified chemical and material inputs used by pesticide manufacturing institutions that are approved by the Ministry of Agriculture.
TABLE-1: Items listed in TABLE-1 are eligible for full exemption from all applicable Customs Duty and Value Added Tax when imported for authorized pesticide production.
TABLE-2: Items listed in TABLE-2 are eligible for a partial exemption from Customs Duty, specifically for the portion of the duty that exceeds fifteen percent.

Pesticide Manufacturer: A pesticide manufacturing company must submit a certificate issued by an official from the Ministry of Agriculture, at least at the rank of Joint Secretary, to the Commissioner of Customs to confirm that imported goods will exclusively be used for pesticide production and packaging.
The company is required to provide a notarized undertaking on a non-judicial stamp paper affirming that imported materials will only be used for agricultural pesticide manufacturing.

In the event of an investigation or complaint by customs or local value-added tax authorities proving that materials were not used for the stated purpose, the manufacturer must pay all applicable duties and taxes on the imported goods.
TABLE-2: Concessional benefits for goods included in this table are restricted to pesticide manufacturers based on their annual import entitlement as approved by the Department of Agricultural Extension.
Customs Duty: Manufacturers are liable to pay all applicable customs duties and other taxes if it is found that imported raw materials were not utilized for the production of agricultural pesticides.
Value Added Tax: Local authorities responsible for this tax may initiate investigations or complaints against pesticide manufacturers if imported goods are misused or diverted from agricultural pesticide production.

Statutory Regulatory Order: This order specifies the legal effective date and the expiration date for the provisions contained within it.

Import Documentation: The declaration requires validation of specific commercial documents including invoice, letter of credit, and transport documents such as bill of lading, airway bill, or truck receipt for imported goods.
Agricultural Pesticides: Imported agricultural pesticides and their packaging materials are eligible for specific treatment when intended to be used as raw materials in agricultural production processes.
The importer must be a recognized entity specifically authorized by the Ministry of Agriculture to manufacture agricultural pesticides.
Ministry of Agriculture: The Ministry of Agriculture acts as the regulatory authority responsible for officially recognizing and authorizing institutions engaged in the manufacturing of agricultural pesticides.

S.R.O. 199-AIN/2025: This order provides customs duty concessions on the import of raw materials and packaging items used for the production of agricultural pesticides.
Importers claiming these duty benefits must sign a declaration pledging to adhere to the terms and conditions prescribed within this instrument.
Customs Authority: The authorities are empowered to demand payment of applicable duties and taxes if imported materials are not used for their intended purpose of pesticide production or if they are diverted for other uses.
They have the legal authority to initiate enforcement actions against importers who violate the conditions set by the National Board of Revenue.
TABLE-1: Importers must strictly comply with the specific conditions and rules imposed by the Commissioner of Customs at the port of entry regarding the goods listed in this table.
TABLE-2: Importers must strictly comply with the specific conditions and rules imposed by the Commissioner of Customs at the port of entry regarding the goods listed in this table.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to issue orders and conditions that importers are legally required to follow under penalty of law.
Customs Act 2023: This Act serves as the legal framework under which customs authorities may take legal action against importers for any breach of the conditions stipulated in the regulatory orders.
